title: Still Waters, Moving Souls
description:
Life is rarely still, yet peace can be found even in the movement. This piece reflects the ebb and flow of life’s currents—moments of uncertainty, moments of grace, and the quiet strength found beneath the surface. Like the ocean, we are constantly changing, yet held by something deeper than ourselves.

That title feels very aligned with your artwork, your MS journey, and the faith-filled, grounded voice that comes through so much of your creative work.

title: Where the Light Breaks Through
description: At first glance, this piece feels like a rupture—an almost violent collision of darkness and colour. The deep blacks sit heavy at the centre, like a void, like a place we don’t often dare to look. But it’s not empty. It’s alive. It’s shifting. The purple pulses around it—rich, royal, unapologetic. It speaks of depth, of identity, of something sacred being formed in the unseen. And then there’s the gold… not placed gently, but fractured, scattered, almost forced into the cracks. As if it didn’t arrive despite the brokenness—but because of it. The texture tells the truth your eyes might miss: this isn’t destruction. This is pressure. This is transformation. This is the moment something caves in… so something greater can rise through it. The hidden message sits right there in the centre: What looks like your breaking point is actually your breakthrough point. This painting doesn’t ask to be understood immediately. It asks to be felt. And when you sit with it long enough, you realise— The darkness isn’t winning. It’s making room for the light.

title: Peace That Stayed
description:
Write up

I used to think the storm meant God had left.

That the chaos, the uncertainty, the pain in my body and the weight in my mind— meant I was somehow drifting further from Him.

Because nothing about this has been calm.

Living in this body… it feels like waves I didn’t ask for.

Symptoms that come without warning. Thoughts that spiral into places I don’t want to go.

A life that doesn’t look like the one I once imagined.

It’s loud.

It’s messy.

It’s exhausting.

And if I’m honest— there have been moments I’ve begged for the storm to just stop.

But it didn’t.

And somewhere in the middle of all of it…

I realised something I didn’t expect—

God didn’t calm the storm straight away.

He met me in it.

Not in the version of me that had it all together, but in the version of me that was tired, overwhelmed, and barely holding on.

That’s where His peace found me.

Not as a feeling that made everything okay— but as something deeper… steadier.

A quiet anchoring in the middle of the noise.

A reminder that even when my world feels out of control,

I am not.

Even when my body feels like it’s fighting against me,

He is still for me.

This kind of peace doesn’t erase the struggle.

It doesn’t take away the grief of what’s been lost.

But it stays.

It holds.

It steadies.

It whispers truth when everything else feels uncertain.

I’m still in the storm.

Some days it still feels heavy.

Some days I still wrestle.

But I’m not searching for peace anymore— because I’ve found it…

right here,

in the middle of it all

title: Blooming Through the Breaking
description:
This piece feels like what resilience looks like when it isn’t neat.

At first glance, it looks vibrant. Bold pinks. Soft golds. Movement. Beauty.

But when I look closer, I see something else.

I see chaos and calm occupying the same space.

I see moments where everything feels like it’s being pulled apart, only to discover something beautiful emerging in the middle of the mess.

Living with MS has taught me that healing rarely arrives in straight lines. It swirls. It twists. It unravels. Some days feel bright and full of possibility, while others feel dark and uncertain. Yet somehow both can exist at the same time.

The deep burgundy shadows in this painting remind me of the hard days, the fear, grief, frustration, and exhaustion that often sit beneath the surface. The vibrant pinks feel like hope refusing to disappear. The gold catches are those unexpected moments of grace that seem to find their way into even the most difficult seasons.

When I painted this, I wasn’t trying to create flowers.

I was simply pouring emotion onto a canvas.

But looking at it now, I see blooms everywhere.

Blooms that weren’t planted in perfect conditions.

Blooms that fought their way through.

And perhaps that’s why this piece resonates with me.

Because life hasn’t unfolded the way I imagined.

MS has broken things open.

Dreams have changed.

Plans have shifted.

Parts of me have been lost.

Yet somehow, in the breaking, something new continues to bloom.

This painting is a reminder that beauty isn’t the absence of struggle.

Sometimes beauty is what grows because of it.

“Blooming Through the Breaking” is about finding colour in the chaos, grace in the grief, and hope in places I never expected it to grow.

title: Beautiful Chaos
description:
Some seasons of life don’t come gently.
They arrive loud, messy, overwhelming and impossible to control.

This piece feels like that.

The black carries the fear, grief and exhaustion that chronic illness can bring.

The electric pink feels like strength refusing to disappear.

And the blue flows through it all like hope… soft, calming, but still fighting for space.

Nothing in this painting sits perfectly still, and honestly, neither do I sometimes.
Living with Multiple Sclerosis can feel exactly like this — emotions colliding, pain mixing with resilience, beauty existing beside heartbreak.

But what I love most is that even in the chaos, the colours still work together.
The broken pieces still create something powerful.

This artwork is a reminder that healing is rarely neat.
Strength doesn’t always look calm.
And even in the middle of uncertainty, there can still be colour, movement, life and beauty.

title: Still Chosen, Still Held
description:
Write up

Some days with MS don’t feel strong.

They feel slow.

Heavy.

Unpredictable.

They feel like waking up and not knowing what version of your body you’re going to get.

Like plans you had… quietly slipping through your hands.

Like your mind running ahead of you, asking questions your heart isn’t ready to answer.

This illness has taken things from me.

Energy.

Clarity.

Pieces of the life I thought I’d be living by now.

And if I’m honest—

there are moments it makes me question everything.

Am I still capable?

Am I still enough?

Am I still… me?

But right in the middle of those thoughts, right when I feel the most unsure, the most shaken- there’s a truth that keeps finding me again:

I am still strong.

Not because I feel it— but because I’m still here, still fighting, still choosing to get up when it would be easier not to.

I am still brave.

Not in big, loud ways— but in the quiet decisions no one sees.

In facing another day inside a body that doesn’t always cooperate.

In not giving up on myself.



And I am still loved.

Not a watered-down, distant kind of love— but a steady, unchanging, God-held kind of love.

The kind that doesn’t disappear when I’m struggling.

The kind that doesn’t depend on how productive I am, or how well I’m coping.

MS may have changed my life—

but it didn’t change that.

So yes…

some days I don’t look like what I thought “strong” would be.

But I’m still standing.

Still showing up.

Still held together by something deeper than what I feel.

And that means… this story isn’t over.

title: Still Blooming Through the Bruise
description:
Reflection: There are parts of grief that don’t arrive quietly.

They crash through you. They stain everything. They leave you trying to recognise yourself in the middle of all the wreckage. 

This piece feels like that tension to me — the collision between pain and survival. The deep crimson carries the weight of suffering, loss, exhaustion and the parts of me that have bled emotionally through this journey with illness, uncertainty and change. 

But then there’s the pink — loud, alive, almost defiant. A reminder that even in the middle of devastation, something inside me still refuses to disappear.

The gold running through the canvas feels sacred somehow. Like all the fractures, grief and disappointments have not just broken me — they’ve revealed me. This painting is about learning that healing is not neat and it is not linear. Sometimes healing looks messy, raw and undone. Sometimes strength looks like simply staying. Simply creating. Simply getting through another day when your body and mind are carrying more than most people can see. And yet somehow, through all of it, there is still beauty here. 

Still colour. Still life. Still me.

title: The Calm that Fought to Stay
description: This piece carries the aftermath of a storm that didn’t ask for permission before it arrived. You can feel it in the movement—every swirl, every fold of colour pulled and stretched like something that’s been shaken to its core. The deep blues crash into each other, heavy and relentless, while the darker voids sit like moments where everything almost gave way. But it didn’t. Because threaded through the chaos… there’s restraint. There’s breath. The softer teals begin to settle the noise, gently pushing back against the turbulence. And then the gold appears—not loud, not overwhelming—but intentional. Like fragments of peace that refused to be swallowed. This isn’t a painting about a storm. It’s about what happens when the storm passes… and you’re still here, trying to steady yourself. The hidden truth lives in the tension between movement and stillness: Calm isn’t the absence of chaos. It’s the decision to soften… while everything inside you is still shaking. This piece holds that moment— right between breaking and becoming still.

title: Falling Into You
description: This piece feels like surrender in its most beautiful and vulnerable form, an unraveling of self in the presence of something deeply consuming. The soft yet striking palette of pinks, mauves, and deep purples creates a dreamlike atmosphere, where emotion flows freely and boundaries begin to dissolve. There is a sense of weightlessness, as though the figure is drifting between control and release, caught in a moment that is both intimate and overwhelming. The intertwining forms and delicate linework suggest connection, hands reaching, holding, perhaps even losing grip. It carries the tension of closeness: the desire to be known fully, paired with the quiet fear of what that exposure brings. The composition draws the eye inward, pulling you into a space where passion and vulnerability exist side by side. This is not just about falling, it is about choosing to fall. To let go, to feel deeply, to be consumed by emotion without resistance. It speaks to the kind of connection that shifts you, softens you, and changes the way you exist within yourself.

title: Where Colour Tries to Remember Light
description: At first, it feels dark—almost impenetrable. Like something closed off… sealed over time. But then the colour starts to speak. Not loudly— not all at once— but in fragments. Small bursts of yellow push through like they’ve fought to be seen. Greens flicker in and out, unsure whether they belong to growth or decay. There are traces of red, almost hidden… like something once vivid that’s now been pressed beneath the surface. Nothing here feels fully certain. The colours don’t sit cleanly—they emerge, hesitate, and sometimes disappear again into the heaviness around them. And yet… they’re still there. It feels like memory. Like moments of light trying to survive inside something that has been weathered, layered, maybe even wounded. You can feel the resistance in the texture— thick, cracked, uneven— as if the surface itself has something to say but won’t give it all away. This piece doesn’t offer resolution. It holds tension. It lives in that quiet question: what remains when brightness doesn’t fully break through… but refuses to disappear?

title: I Disappeared to Survive
description: This piece doesn’t scream. It buries. Layer after layer, it folds in on itself—dark greens, bruised blues, shadows swallowing shape. Nothing here is clean. Nothing is easy to read. And that’s the truth of it… because this wasn’t made in clarity. This was made in survival. There are no open spaces—only movement, tension, hiding. Like something trying to stay unseen. Like a soul that learned it was safer to blend in than to be exposed. The black isn’t just darkness. It’s protection. It’s the parts of you that said, “If I stay small, I’ll stay safe.” But look closer. There are flashes—sharp, almost defiant streaks of blue and teal cutting through the weight. They don’t ask permission to be there. They break through. Quietly, but undeniably. That’s the truth hidden in this piece: You didn’t disappear because you were weak. You disappeared because you had to survive what tried to erase you. And even here—buried, layered, almost lost— you’re still showing up. Not loudly. Not perfectly. But enough to prove… you were never gone.

title: She Moves Like Water
description:
There’s something about her… you don’t see it all at once—
you feel it. 
She isn’t still. 

She was never meant to be. 

She moves through this piece like water— soft in one moment, overwhelming in the next. 

Flowing, folding, stretching herself into spaces that don’t always make sense… but somehow still hold her. 

The blues carry a depth that isn’t just colour— it’s emotion. 

It’s the quiet kind of heavy. 

The kind you sit in, not run from.  

And then there’s the gold—
 
not loud, 
not demanding— but breaking through like truth. 

Like those moments where something inside her says, “Even here… I’m still here.” 

You can feel the push and pull. 

The surrender and the fight. 

The way she lets go in one breath and gathers herself in the next.  

Nothing about this is forced. 

It’s movement born from feeling. 

Emotion  that didn’t have words, so it found another way out. 

And maybe that’s what she is now— not fixed, 
not certain, 
not who she once was… 

but something fluid. 

Something evolving. 

Something that refuses to stay stuck.  

She moves. 
She shifts. 
She becomes. 

And in all that motion— there’s something powerful in her… because she didn’t break. 

 She flowed

title: Veins of Gold in Violet Chaos
description: This piece feels like a storm that refuses to dim, an emotional landscape where deep violets swirl and collide, carrying both weight and movement. The richness of purple evokes introspection, depth, and a kind of quiet resilience, while the bursts of gold cut through like light breaking into darkness. Rather than overpowering, the gold feels earned, like moments of clarity, strength, or hope emerging from within the turbulence. There is a beautiful tension here between control and surrender. The fluid motion suggests letting go, allowing the paint to find its own path, while the layered textures and splatters hint at complexity beneath the surface, thoughts, feelings, and experiences that do not sit still. The white flecks almost read like stars or energy, giving the work a sense of expansiveness, as though it stretches beyond the canvas. Altogether, it tells a story of navigating chaos while still holding onto something luminous. It is not about escaping the storm, it is about discovering that even within it, there are veins of something powerful, radiant, and unbreakable.

title: “Held in the Mess”
description:
This one isn’t clean.
It’s not controlled.
It didn’t ask for permission to come together the way it did.

It just… happened.

Gold pushing through black like something refusing to stay buried.
Grey cutting through the middle like the in-between—
not broken, not whole… just existing.

There’s tension in it.
You can feel it.

Like two parts of you pulling in different directions—
one trying to rise,
one trying to shut everything down.

And neither one wins.
They just learn to live on the same canvas.

That’s what this is.

Not balance.
Not peace.

But coexistence.

It’s the reality of holding strength and struggle
in the same breath.

Of showing up when things feel heavy,
when your head’s loud,
when your body doesn’t quite feel like yours.

It’s not pretty…
but it’s real.

And the gold?

That’s the part of you that keeps showing up anyway.

title: Painting 3
description: Artwork details to be added later.

title: I Am Becoming
description: This piece speaks in quiet strength, not loud perfection. It doesn’t demand that you have everything figured out—it simply asks you to stand where you are and claim who you are becoming. “I am” is not just a statement. It’s a declaration of identity, a reclaiming of voice, a refusal to be defined by doubt, fear, or past versions of yourself. Every stroke, every space, every imperfection in this piece reminds you that growth is not linear—it’s layered, textured, and real. You are not behind. You are not lacking. You are not too much or not enough. You are becoming. “I am strong.” “I am worthy.” “I am healing.” “I am still rising.” Let this piece be a mirror—not of who you were, but of who you are choosing to be. A daily reminder that your words shape your world, and your identity is not something you wait to discover… it’s something you speak into existence.

title: Spirit beneath the Ashes
description: For a long time, I couldn’t connect with this piece. It felt distant, almost out of reach. But when I finally did, I saw something I hadn’t noticed before, the reflection of the battle I’ve been living with for six years, fighting a chronic illness every single day. And in that moment, this painting became more than colors on canvas, it became a mirror. I could see her: the warrior woman within me, standing strong despite everything. "I don’t look like everything I’ve walked through. I’ve fought battle after battle and I’m still standing. I’ve cried more tears than I can count and yet my smile hasn’t faded. I’ve survived things meant to break me and I’m still breathing. I’m a warrior, not because of my own strength, but because of Him living in me. Every fight, every scar, every victory belongs to the Lord."

title: Veil of Agony
description: This painting captures the raw, unflinching humanity of Jesus in His crucifixion. Against a deep, dark blue background, His face reflects profound agony — a moment of suffering that transcends time and touches the soul. The imperfections in the print are not flaws; they are testimony to the reality of His sacrifice, reminding us that pain, struggle, and the brokenness of the world are part of the path toward redemption. This piece invites reflection, empathy, and a tangible encounter with the weight of love poured out for humanity.

title: Distant Tide
description: This piece captures the feeling of the ocean not as a place, but as an emotion deep, vast, and out of reach. Dark, moody tones hold the canvas like still water at dusk, while currents of gold and green drift through on one side, searching for light. On the other, a surge of violet rises with raw intensity, textured and restless, like emotion pushing to the surface. The movement throughout feels like waves beneath the surface unsettled, powerful, and alive, expressing a quiet tension between longing and release, as if the ocean itself is being felt from afar rather than touched.

title: Ignition of the Soul
description: This piece burns with an undeniable intensity, an eruption of fiery passion that refuses to be contained. The sweeping forms feel like flames in motion, petals or embers rising and folding into one another, alive with energy and purpose. Deep reds and molten oranges dominate the canvas, creating a heat that is both consuming and transformative, while flashes of gold cut through like sparks, moments of brilliance born from the blaze. There is no stillness here. Every movement feels charged, as though the painting is driven by something raw and deeply felt. It speaks to a passion that is not quiet or controlled, but fierce, instinctive, and unapologetic. The layers build upon one another like waves of emotion, intensity, desire, strength, all colliding and expanding outward. Rather than destruction, the fire here represents becoming. It is the kind of passion that reshapes, that demands to be seen, that refuses to dim. This painting captures that exact moment where feeling turns into force, where something inside ignites and begins to glow with unstoppable power.

title: Suffering and Transcendence
description: This piece feels like a moment suspended between suffering and transcendence. At its center, the face of Jesus Christ emerges, not just as a figure, but as a presence. The features are marked by the weight of crucifixion: pain etched into the brow, heaviness in the eyes, a quiet surrender in the mouth. There is a human fragility here, something deeply tangible, skin, strain, exhaustion, yet it is held with a stillness that feels almost sacred. The orange-red background burns like a living force. It evokes fire, blood, and the raw intensity of sacrifice. This is not a passive backdrop, it feels like emotion itself, like the atmosphere of anguish, love, and transformation all at once. The warmth of the tones carries both violence and divinity, suggesting that suffering and redemption are intertwined rather than separate. Spiritually, the painting speaks of endurance, the kind that does not resist pain but moves through it. There is a sense that this face is not only looking outward, but inward, as if holding the burden of humanity while also offering a quiet, unwavering compassion. Tangibly, the texture of the paint likely moves in unpredictable directions, thick in places, almost restless, mirroring the chaos of the moment. Yet the face anchors it all, becoming a focal point of calm within intensity. It is as if the physical act of painting itself became a form of release, each stroke carrying emotion from the artist into the canvas. Overall, the piece feels like fire meeting stillness, pain meeting purpose. It does not just depict crucifixion; it embodies the emotional and spiritual weight of it, inviting the viewer to sit inside that tension rather than look away from it.

title: Where Fire Meets Flesh
description: This piece does not sit quietly, it burns. Every stroke feels like it has been pulled straight from the artist's chest, raw and unfiltered. There is a tension here, a push and pull between control and surrender, where the paint seems to move with a life of its own. The heat in the tones speaks of something deeper than colour, it is emotion at its most exposed. Passion, struggle, longing, all colliding in a single moment. You can feel the artist not just painting, but releasing, letting something internal rise to the surface, unapologetically. There is a human quality embedded in the work, something almost tangible. It feels like skin, like breath, like presence. The textures carry movement, like a story unfolding in real time, one that has not been polished or softened, but left honest. This is not just a visual experience. It is a confrontation. A moment where emotion refuses to stay hidden and instead, demands to be seen.

title: Where I Still Grow
description:
here’s a quiet honesty in this piece…

the kind that doesn’t beg to be noticed,

but stays with you anyway.



Nothing here is perfect.

Some stems lean, some feel fragile,

some stand tall like they’ve earned their place.

And yet—together—they belong.



That’s what hits the deepest.



It feels like life…

not the polished version,

but the real one.



The one where parts of you are still blooming,

while other parts feel worn, tired…

maybe even a little forgotten.



There’s softness in the whites,

warmth in the yellows,

and then those small bursts of colour—

like moments of joy that show up

even when you didn’t think they would.



And the background—

that open blue—

it feels like space.

Like breath.

Like permission to just be

without needing to explain where you’re at.



This piece doesn’t fight for perfection.

It allows contrast.

It allows unevenness.

It allows growth in all its stages.



And maybe that’s the emotion that settles in…



That you don’t have to have it all together

to still be growing.



That even in the mess,

in the in-between,

in the parts of you that feel unsure—



there is still life.

There is still beauty.

There is still something in you

reaching toward the light

title: The Lion Within
description:
This piece is deeply personal.

When people look at a lion, they often see strength, courage, power, and confidence.

What they don’t always see is the battle that strength was forged through.

Living with MS has taught me that courage isn’t about never being afraid. It’s about getting up every day and facing uncertainty anyway. It’s about continuing to move forward when your body and your mind are telling you two different stories.

The lion in this painting represents that part of me.

The part that has cried.

The part that has questioned.

The part that has grieved the life I thought I would have.

And the part that keeps showing up anyway.

The deep blues speak to me of the darker seasons—the loneliness, the fear, the nights spent wondering what comes next. But blue is also the colour of hope, faith, healing, and depth. It reminds me that some of life’s greatest growth happens beneath the surface where nobody else can see it.

The gold surrounding the lion feels like God’s presence.

Not removing the struggle.

Not taking away the diagnosis.

But surrounding me with grace in the middle of it.

The gold is a reminder that even the broken places can shine.

That strength can coexist with vulnerability.

That courage doesn’t roar all the time.

Sometimes courage whispers:

“Get up and try again tomorrow.”

This painting isn’t about being fearless.

It’s about being faithful.

It’s about discovering that true strength is not found in what we can control, but in what we choose to trust when everything feels uncertain.

For me, this lion is not a symbol of power over others.

It is a symbol of perseverance.

Of resilience.

Of quiet determination.

Of a woman who has been shaken, stretched, challenged and changed, but who refuses to surrender her spirit.

Because the greatest lion I have met is not the one on this canvas.

It is the one that lives within.

“The Lion Within” is a reflection of faith, resilience, and the unbreakable spirit that continues to rise, even on the hardest days.
